title: Microsoft Teams: organisation evaluation score for third-party apps and agents
summary: The briefing passes: its admin paths, PowerShell operation, licensing treatment and roadmap facts are supported. Narrow the promise that editing requirements recalculates every score; Microsoft documents a change to the calculation, not a universal recalculation guarantee.

claims.claim: The evaluation criteria page is Teams admin center > Teams apps > Evaluation score settings.
claims.quote: Sign in to Microsoft Teams admin center. In the left navigation, go to Teams apps. Select Evaluation score settings.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no PowerShell, Graph or other API that configures these evaluation criteria.

Read feature page and results.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival if no administrator configures evaluation score settings.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Evaluation score settings default automatically configured. Read roadmap description, org-trust-standard, and the Trust Score entries in teams-admin and governmentchannel; none states the initial configuration or score display when nobody configures requirements.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included under the product's existing Teams licence, with no feature-specific entitlement published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Users generally need a Teams license to use Teams.
claims.quote: You manage access to Teams at the user level by assigning or removing a Microsoft Teams product license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Joining Teams meetings anonymously is an exception to the user Teams-license requirement.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: No licence or add-on specific to evaluation scores is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams evaluation score license pricing meter. Read org-trust-standard, user-access and the Overview of all add-on licenses in microsoft-teams-add-on-licensing; none names an evaluation-score licence or add-on.

claims.claim: No price or meter specific to evaluation scores is published in the feature documentation or found by targeted search.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams evaluation score license pricing meter. Read org-trust-standard, user-access, Teams add-on licensing overview and search results; no feature price or meter appeared. Teams interoperability pricing results describe communication APIs, not evaluation criteria.

claims.claim: Evaluation score settings offers a predefined requirement list.
claims.quote: Review the predefined list of available security, compliance, and permission related requirements.

claims.claim: Admins can add evaluation requirements and save their selection.
claims.quote: On the Evaluation score settings page, select Add. The Add a requirement page opens and displays a list of predefined security, compliance, and permission related requirements to choose from. Select Save to save the selected requirements.

claims.claim: Admins can edit evaluation requirements.
claims.quote: On the Evaluation score settings page, select the requirement you want to change. Select Edit. Make the necessary changes and select Save.

claims.claim: Admins can remove evaluation requirements.
claims.quote: On the Evaluation score settings page, select the requirement you want to remove. Select the remove icon.

claims.claim: Admins can download the selected requirements as CSV.
claims.quote: Admins can download the finalized set of organization requirements from the Evaluation score settings page. On the Evaluation score settings page, select the excel icon. Listed requirements will be downloaded in the CSV format.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Configured requirements drive the new Evaluation score column on Manage apps.
claims.quote: Based on the requirements that are configured on the Evaluation score settings page, your organization specific evaluation score is made available through a new Evaluation score column in the Manage apps page in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The score is the percentage of selected requirements met by an eligible app or agent.
claims.quote: The Evaluation score column shows the percentage of selected requirements that are met for each eligible app or agent.

claims.claim: Admins can sort apps and agents by evaluation score.
claims.quote: Apps and agents are sorted by their evaluation score in ascending or descending order, based on count of requirements that are met.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Manage apps has an Evaluation requirements met filter.
claims.quote: On the Manage apps page, select the Filter icon. Select Evaluation requirements met value from the Filter dropdown.

claims.claim: The evaluation filter supports greater than or equal to a specified percentage as separate conditions.
claims.quote: Choose one of the following conditions: Greater than a specified percentage; Equal to a specified percentage.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Selecting an app or agent under Teams apps > Manage apps leads to its details page and Evaluation score report tab.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Teams apps > Manage apps. Select an app or agent. On the app details page, review the Evaluation score shown on the app card. Select the Evaluation score report tab.

claims.claim: The report identifies each configured requirement by name.
claims.quote: Name: The configured requirement.

claims.claim: The report shows each requirement's configured value.
claims.quote: Requirement value: The configured value of the requirement.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Met, Not met and No data are distinct requirement statuses in the report.
claims.quote: Status: Whether the requirement is Met, Not met, or No data, based on the underlying metadata.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: A configured parameter unavailable for an app or agent receives No data rather than Not met.
claims.quote: If a configured security, compliance, permission related parameter isn't available for the selected app or agent, the status is shown as no data.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: What is scored
claims.claim: Only third-party apps and agents are eligible for evaluation scores.
claims.quote: Evaluation scores are shown only for apps and agents that meet all of the following conditions: The app or agent is a third-party application

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: What is scored
claims.claim: Score eligibility requires security and compliance data to be available.
claims.quote: Evaluation scores are shown only for apps and agents that meet all of the following conditions: ... Security and compliance data is available for the app

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope
claims.claim: Apps already made available in the organization for anyone to install or use are outside the scoring conditions.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure

claims.quote: Evaluation scores reflect the security, compliance, permissions related metadata currently available

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Scores may change when underlying app or agent data changes.

claims.claim: Adding, editing or removing requirements changes how scores are calculated.

claims.claim: Changing requirements does not change the app's or agent's underlying security, compliance or permission data.
claims.quote: It doesn't change the underlying security, compliance, permission related data provided by the app or agent.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: The score and report inform an admin decision rather than themselves constituting app approval.
claims.quote: This detailed view helps admins understand exactly which requirements an app or agent satisfies and where gaps exist before deciding whether to make the app or agent available in the organization.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: The existing allow or block control manages individual app or agent availability separately from score review.
claims.quote: You can allow or block specific agents and apps on either the Manage apps page or in the app details page.

claims.claim: The allow or block route is Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <Boolean> changes the app's tenant state.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <String> [-IsBlocked <Boolean>] ... -Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app. -IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Before unified app management migration, app allow or block settings must be synchronized across Teams admin center and Microsoft 365 admin center Integrated apps.
claims.quote: If your organization isn't migrated to unified app management, allow or block the agent or app in Teams admin center and under the Integrated apps page in Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The feature's Learn page does not describe reading organizational content.
claims.quote: Searched: organizational content, data, metadata in the full org-trust-standard page. It describes security, compliance and permission metadata and does not describe reading tenant content.

claims.claim: The feature's Learn page describes no change for end users.
claims.quote: Searched: end users, users, availability in the full org-trust-standard page. It describes admin settings, a Manage apps column, filters and a report before an admin availability decision; no end-user experience change is described.

claims.claim: Editing or removing a requirement recalculates every score.
claims.quote: Searched: Evaluation score Teams recalculate. Read org-trust-standard and returned excerpts. Microsoft states that changes alter how scores are calculated, but does not state that every score is recalculated.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with 'Review the requirement list when policy changes, because editing or removing a requirement changes how evaluation scores are calculated.' https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/org-trust-standard

claims.claim: The allow or block row governs availability, not the evaluation criteria or score calculation.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows administrators to modify app state, availability and installation status by adding or removing users and groups or changing assignment type or installation status.

claims.claim: The evaluation criteria are organizational, tenant-scoped requirements.
claims.quote: admins can define an organization’s app approval criteria and use it to evaluate apps or agents before allowing them in their tenant.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist tells admins to check org-wide app settings and app-centric user access, but those distinct controls have no table rows.
claims.quote: Use Manage apps for allow or block decisions, checking org-wide app settings and app-centric user access as well; ... The table has only evaluation requirements and individual app Allow or Block rows.
claims.fix: Remove 'checking org-wide app settings and app-centric user access as well' from the At rollout checklist bullet. Keep these verified prerequisites in the existing allow or block row's note and Governance controls prose; do not add rows.
